TravClan, a traveltech startup, has raised $5 million in funding from Flipkart and August One, along with debt financing from Trifecta Capital. The startup said it will use the funds to expand its global supply network, enhance its technology and AI capabilities, and strengthen destination operations across key international markets. TravClan provides a technology platform that integrates supply, technology and fulfilment infrastructure for travel businesses. Its platform supports various functions, including pricing, itinerary creation, bookings, payments, fulfilment, customer communication and on-ground support. The startup helps travel businesses sell and fulfil bookings for flights, hotels, activities and international holiday packages. “Our ambition is to make TravClan the infrastructure that any travel business can build on instead of having to recreate the entire travel stack itself. This capital allows us to invest aggressively behind that opportunity,” said TravClan co-founder & CEO Arun Bagaria. According to TravClan, it enables travel agents to plan, price and rebuild complex international itineraries in a shorter period of time. It also brings global inventory, pricing, booking, AI-powered workflows and destination fulfillment into one platform. TravClan claims more than 15,000 travel agents across India use their platform to book flights, hotels, activities and destination services processing more than $100 million in annual travel sales. Around 40% of the company’s business now originates from Tier II and Tier III cities, reflecting the growing demand for international travel beyond India’s largest metros. “TravClan has built a capital efficient model by owning supply rather than buying demand, and distributing through agents in underserved markets,” said Sahil Kukreja, Vice President, Trifecta Capital. “We backed them when owning supply looked like the slow way to build. leads.posting: Forward deployed AI startup AuxoAI raises $20.7 Mn in Series A round led by NTTVC. Forward deployed AI company AuxoAI has raised $20.7 million in a Series A funding round led by NTTVC, a Silicon Valley based venture capital firm backed by Japanese technology conglomerate NTT. The round also saw participation from George Still Jr., Amit Zavery and Giacomo Sonnino. Earlier this year, AuxoAI was named one of the select AI Pureplay Partners at Google Next as part of Google’s $750 million investment in enterprise AI deployment. The company will use the fresh funds to expand its global forward deployed teams, invest in proprietary technology and AI native delivery capabilities, and scale its presence and strategic ecosystem, AuxoAI said in a press release. Founded in 2023 by Amaresh Tripathy, Arvinder Pal Singh and Kabir Singh, AuxoAI works with large global enterprises to identify AI use cases, redesign workflows and build production ready systems aimed at delivering measurable business outcomes. The company deploys teams of AI strategists and engineers who work alongside clients to understand their business operations, identify opportunities for AI adoption and develop systems for use in production environments. AuxoAI also offers Damia, its proprietary forward deployed engineering (FDE) workbench, which it says incorporates learnings from multiple enterprise AI deployments to accelerate implementation. The company is a Google Gemini Enterprise transformation partner and an AWS Advanced Tier partner. AuxoAI works with enterprise customers, including UKG and Fogo de Chão.

leads.posting: Rural healthcare startup CureBay raises Rs 100 Cr in Pre-Series C led by IvyCap. CureBay, a rural healthcare startup, has raised around Rs 100 crore in a Pre-Series C funding round led by IvyCap Ventures. The round comprises Rs 69 crore in equity from IvyCap Ventures and existing investors, along with over Rs 30 crore in debt from Trifecta Capital, Alteria Capital and VentureSoul Partners. The proceeds will be used to expand its presence across India, including an entry into Andhra Pradesh. The company also plans to strengthen its technology and artificial intelligence capabilities to improve health screening, patient insights and clinical decision making. Founded in 2021 by Priyadarshi Mohapatra, Shobhan Mahapatra and Sanjay Swain, CureBay operates a network of technology enabled clinics that provide healthcare services in underserved areas. Its services include doctor consultations, medicines, diagnostic tests, surgery facilitation and annual health memberships. The company operates over 250 clinics across seven states, supported by more than 1,800 Swasthya Mitras, 530 trained clinical staff, 230 doctor partners and over 210 partner hospitals and laboratories. It has served more than 17 lakh patients and conducts over 400 health camps every month. CureBay operates a six layer rural healthcare system that combines physical clinics, a community health worker network, a digital platform, AI powered screening, a 24/7 command centre and CureBay Kavach. The company also works with the government on healthcare delivery initiatives and has been named the healthcare partner for Samriddhi Kendra, a Government of India initiative. CureBay last raised $21 million in a Series B round led by Bertelsmann India Investments in May 2025. Existing investor Elevar Equity and British International Investment also participated in the round.

leads.posting: Vectorial raises $3 Mn led by SenseAI Ventures. Vectorial, an AI startup building human behaviour simulation tools for product development, has raised $3 million in a funding round led by SenseAI Ventures. Other participants include Smilegate, Berkeley SkyDeck, Berkeley AI Research Lab, Dent Capital, Motus Ventures, SUM Ventures and angel investors, including product leaders from Meta, Shopify and Mastercard. Founded by Taranveer Singh, Rahul Garg and Jasmine Kaur, Vectorial helps companies predict how users may respond to software products, digital experiences and marketing campaigns. Its platform uses AI simulations to test product ideas without relying solely on traditional surveys and interviews. The company claims that it has modelled more than 2.5 million people globally, including 500,000 in India, and conducted over 30,000 simulations. Its customers include boAt, GoodRx, Suki AI, Everkind and Concrete Software, across sectors such as healthcare, gaming and e-commerce. Vectorial’s SAPIENS model uses socio-demographic, psychographic and behavioural data to simulate target audiences across web, mobile and AI-based applications. The company claims its model is 30% more accurate at predicting human behaviour than general-purpose large language models. Its simulations reproduce findings from previous user studies with over 85% accuracy. According to the company, customers run around 600 simulations per month, equivalent to approximately 40 user studies, and conduct up to 20 times more research than before.
